Technical FAQ

Engineering-focused answers for API behavior, auth boundaries, deployment posture, frontend rendering, and simulation data flow.

API & Simulation

Which endpoint powers the Strategy Variants panel?
The panel is fed by POST /api/v1/strategy/full-simulate, which returns multi-variant outputs including pit laps, risk level, and finish probabilities. The UI keeps mock fallback rendering if the call fails.

Why might variants stay static for some users?
Common causes include stale deployment artifacts, client cache, auth token expiration, or effect dependency bugs in the view lifecycle. Ensure the frontend build containing variant-fetch integration is deployed and hard-refresh cache.

How should win probability be interpreted?
It is scenario-derived from simulation runs, not certainty. Use it comparatively across proposed plans and combine with risk-level and operational context (traffic, degradation trend, safety car odds).

Auth & Permissions

Which endpoints are protected by auth?
Core strategy, model, and race-state endpoints require current-user dependency checks. Role-based checks further restrict sensitive operations so read-only roles cannot trigger privileged strategy actions.

Why does an endpoint return 401 vs 403?
401 indicates missing/invalid authentication. 403 indicates authenticated but insufficient role/permission for that operation.

Frontend Reliability & Accessibility

What caused the “Cannot access before initialization” crash?
A temporal-dead-zone reference in a hook dependency chain can trigger this class of error after minification. The fix is to avoid referencing values before declaration and keep effect dependencies stable and explicit.

How is seizure-risk visual intensity reduced?
The animated grid uses lower-opacity accents, slower movement, and reduced-motion preference support. This lowers flicker perception while preserving design identity.

Why are select options sometimes invisible on Windows?
Native form controls can ignore inherited text color under certain themes or forced-color modes. Explicit select/option color backgrounds and forced-color handling improve consistency.

Cookies & Consent

How is cookie consent persisted?
Consent state is persisted in local storage under a dedicated key. The footer trigger dispatches a cookie-settings event, allowing users to reopen consent controls and reject optional cookies later.

What is the expected reject behavior?
Selecting reject should store a declined state and disable optional tracking behavior for subsequent client-side events. Essential functionality should remain unaffected.

Deployment Notes

We deploy on GCP, not Vercel. What changes operationally?
Your source branch and build/deploy chain should target GCP artifact + hosting/runtime. Frontend fixes must be pulled into that pipeline branch and deployed through your GCP process to be visible in production.

How to validate post-deploy quickly?
  • Open strategy view and confirm variants change with race/driver input.
  • Open footer cookie settings and verify Reject Optional is available.
  • Check dropdown readability on Windows in light mode.
  • Verify animation is calmer and honors reduced-motion preference.
